messages.content:
Work out the ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Think in three steps: first name the condition chiefly responsible for the admission, second name the ICD-10-AM chapter letter it belongs to, third give the three-character category.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: Irreversible airflow limitation in a heavy smoker with an infective exacerbation is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, chapter J, category J44.
CODE: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: ST elevation with a rising troponin and culprit-vessel stenting is an acute myocardial infarction, chapter I, category I21.
CODE: I21

Hospital course:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY:

Patient Name: [REDACTED]
Gender: Female
Age: 70 years old

Admission Date: [REDACTED]
Discharge Date: [REDACTED]

Hospital Course:
The patient was admitted with worsening right upper quadrant pain, anorexia, and 10 lb weight loss. A CT scan revealed hepatomegaly and several hypodense lesions consistent with liver metastases, indicating recurrent/metastatic disease. The patient was started on pembrolizumab and axitinib as first-line therapy for her condition.

During treatment, the patient experienced side effects and required a dose reduction of axitinib due to fatigue. Elevated thyroid stimulating hormone levels were also monitored and subsequently managed with medication.

After 12 weeks of combination axitinib/pembrolizumab, repeat CT scans showed progression of liver metastases, prompting a liver biopsy.

Genomic testing revealed loss of function mutations in von Hippel-Lindau (VHL) and BRCA1-associated protein (BAP1) genes, as well as copy-number loss of cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitor 2A (CDKN2A).

The patient was discharged home with appropriate follow-up measures.
Diagnoses: [diagnosis section withheld]
Procedures:
1. CT-guided liver biopsy

Updated Medications:
None.

Follow-up Care:
The patient will receive appropriate follow-up care as recommended by her healthcare provider.

Write your reasoning in at most three short sentences, then a final line of exactly 'CODE: <letter><digit><digit>'.

text:
**Condition:** This is recurrent clear-cell renal cell carcinoma (VHL loss, axitinib/pembrolizumab) presenting as liver metastases. The admission care, including CT-guided liver biopsy, was directed at the secondary liver malignancy rather than the previously treated primary.
**Chapter:** C (neoplasms).
**Category:** secondary malignant neoplasm of liver, C78. This rests on assuming the kidney primary was already treated; if the admission were directed at the kidney tumour itself, the category would be C64.

CODE: C78
